I'll be thorough but focused on the 3-4 page target for a moderate difficulty fixture.# Accessibility Design Plan: Animated Page Transition > **For Claude:** Use a11y-planner protocol. Review with a11y-critic after implementation. > **Compliance target:** WCAG 2.2 AA > **Users who need accessibility:** Screen reader users (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver), keyboard-only users, motion-sensitive/vestibular disorder users, low vision users > **Assistive technologies:** NVDA (Windows), JAWS (Windows), VoiceOver (macOS), keyboard-only navigation **Feature:** A page transition system in a React SPA using framer-motion that animates route changes with slide (300ms) and fade (200ms) variants. The outgoing page slides out while the incoming page slides in simultaneously, creating DOM overlap during transitions. **Risk Level:** Medium — two independent concerns: motion sensitivity compliance (WCAG 2.3.3) and post-navigation focus management (WCAG 2.4.3), plus a DOM-overlap problem where both old and new pages coexist in the accessibility tree during animation. --- ## Scope & Context ### What is being built A `PageTransition` wrapper component applied to all routes in a React SPA using React Router v6 and framer-motion's `AnimatePresence`. Two transition variants: "slide" (outgoing slides left, incoming slides right, 300ms) and "fade" (cross-dissolve, 200ms). The route change itself is instant — no server fetch delay. ### User needs - **Motion-sensitive users:** Need the ability to disable or reduce animation intensity via `prefers-reduced-motion` system preference without losing functionality. - **Screen reader users:** Must not encounter content from both old and new pages simultaneously during transition; must be clearly informed when navigation is complete. - **Keyboard-only users:** Focus must move to a meaningful location on the new page after navigation, not remain trapped in exiting (now visually hidden) content. ### Compliance target WCAG 2.2 AA. Key criteria: SC 2.3.3 (Animation from Interactions), SC 2.4.3 (Focus Order), SC 2.2.2 (Pause, Stop, Hide — noted for distinction), SC 1.4.13 (Content on Hover or Focus — not directly applicable but relevant to transition timing). ### Assistive technologies NVDA (Windows), JAWS (Windows), VoiceOver (macOS), keyboard-only navigation users. ### Existing code context framer-motion `AnimatePresence` is already implemented for the slide animation. No `prefers-reduced-motion` detection exists. No post-navigation focus management exists — focus remains wherever it was before navigation, which may be on an element now in the exiting/hidden page. ### Constraints - framer-motion must remain as the animation library - Animation durations are designer-specified: 300ms (slide), 200ms (fade) - Both variants must be supported - Route change is instant (no server fetch delay to mask transition timing) --- ## Semantic Structure Plan ### Landmark structure during transitions The `PageTransition` component itself does not introduce new landmarks — it wraps the existing page content. However, because `AnimatePresence` with default ("sync") mode keeps exiting pages in the DOM while incoming pages render simultaneously, we must ensure only ONE page is exposed to the accessibility tree at any time. ### Document outline Each individual route/page maintains its own semantic structure (h1 → h2 hierarchy, main landmark, etc.). The transition wrapper does not alter this — it only manages visibility and focus during state changes between pages. ### Structure diagram ```html

Previous Page Title

...content...

New Page Title

...content...
Navigated to: New Page Title
``` ### WCAG citations - **SC 1.3.1 Info and Relationships:** Each page maintains proper heading hierarchy and landmark structure; the transition wrapper does not disrupt this. - **SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value:** The route announcer region has a clear role (status/announcement) via `aria-live`. --- ## Interaction Pattern Design ### Nature of interaction Unlike traditional interactive widgets (buttons, menus, dialogs), the page transition is not directly controlled by keyboard input — it's triggered by navigation actions (clicking links, browser back/forward). However, there are two critical interaction concerns: 1. **Motion preference detection:** The system must detect `prefers-reduced-motion` and adjust animation behavior accordingly before any transition occurs. 2. **Post-transition state:** After the transition completes, focus management determines where keyboard/screen reader users land on the new page. ### APG pattern mapping This component does not map to a specific APG interactive widget pattern (it's not a dialog, menu, tab panel, etc.). Instead, it relates to two broader accessibility concepts: 1. **Motion animation reduction** — Related to WCAG SC 2.3.3 and the [APG Motion Animation Guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/motion-sensitivity/). 2. **SPA navigation focus management** — Related to the APG [Managing Focus in Single Page Applications](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/) guidance and the general principle that focus should follow content changes (SC 2.4.3). ### Keyboard interaction model - **Tab:** Standard tab order within each page is unaffected by transitions. After navigation completes, Tab moves through elements on the NEW page only. - **Shift+Tab:** Reverse tab order works normally on the new page after transition. - **Escape:** Not applicable to route transitions (no modal or overlay to dismiss). However, if a user navigates away while focused on an element in the old page, focus must move to the new page — Escape is not used for this. - **Arrow keys / Enter / Space:** These trigger navigation actions (clicking links), which then initiate the transition. The transition itself does not respond to keyboard input during animation. ### Screen reader behavior expectations - During exit animation: Only the incoming (new) page should be in the accessibility tree. The exiting page must have `aria-hidden="true"`. - After transition completes: Screen reader announces "Navigated to [page title]" via an aria-live region, and focus is on the new page's main content area. ### WCAG citations - **SC 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions:** User-triggered animations (route transitions) must respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. If the user has set this preference, motion animation triggered by interaction can be disabled. - **SC 2.4.3 Focus Order:** After navigation, focus must move to a meaningful location on the new page in a logical order. --- ## Focus Management Plan ### The core problem After a route transition completes: 1. The old page's content is visually hidden (or removed from DOM) but may still contain focusable elements that are now invisible. 2. Keyboard focus remains wherever it was before navigation — potentially on an element in the exiting/hidden page. 3. Screen reader users have no announcement that a new page has loaded unless we explicitly provide one. ### Focus strategy: Move to main content heading after transition **Primary mechanism:** After the incoming page's enter animation completes, move focus to the `
` element (or its first heading) of the new page. This is the standard SPA navigation pattern recommended by WAI-ARIA APG and ensures screen reader users immediately know they are on a new page. Implementation approach: 1. Give the `
` element `tabindex="-1"` so it can receive programmatic focus without adding it to the tab order. 2. After framer-motion's enter animation completes (using `onAnimationComplete` callback), call `.focus()` on the main element of the new page. 3. This ensures keyboard and screen reader users land at the top of the new page content, not stranded in invisible exiting content. ### Secondary mechanism: Route announcer via aria-live **Supplementary announcement:** Use an `aria-live="polite"` region to announce "Navigated to [page title]" when a route change occurs. This provides additional context for screen reader users who may benefit from knowing the page name explicitly, especially if they were not actively focused on a link before navigation (e.g., browser back button). ```html
Navigated to: New Page Title
``` ### DOM overlap handling during transition **Critical issue:** With framer-motion's `AnimatePresence` in default ("sync") mode, both the exiting and incoming pages exist in the DOM simultaneously. This means screen readers could potentially read content from BOTH pages during the ~300ms transition window. **Solution:** Apply `aria-hidden="true"` to the exiting page element while its exit animation is running. Remove it (or let framer-motion remove the element) when the exit completes. The incoming page should NOT have `aria-hidden` — it must be fully accessible during and after its enter animation. Implementation approach: - Use framer-motion's `onExitComplete` or a custom callback to manage aria-hidden state on exiting elements. - Alternatively, use React state to track which page key is "active" (not hidden) and apply aria-hidden conditionally based on whether the element's key matches the active route. ### Focus trap considerations No focus trap is needed for route transitions — this is not a modal or overlay pattern. However, we must ensure that: - During transition, focusable elements in the exiting page are NOT reachable via Tab (achieved by `aria-hidden="true"` on the exiting container). - After transition completes, only the new page's interactive elements are in the tab order. ### Skip link considerations The existing skip-to-content link should continue to work after navigation — it jumps to `#main-content` or similar anchor. Since each page has its own `
` element with a consistent ID pattern (or we use `tabindex="-1"` on main), the skip link will correctly jump to the new page's content area regardless of which route is active. ### WCAG citations - **SC 2.4.3 Focus Order:** Focus must move logically after navigation — landing on the new page's main content, not remaining in invisible exiting content. - **SC 2.1.1 Keyboard:** All functionality (navigation) must be available via keyboard; focus management ensures this works correctly post-transition. --- ## State Communication Design ### States during route transition lifecycle | State | Duration | Visual Representation | Screen Reader Experience | Programmatic Handling | WCAG Citation | |-------|----------|----------------------|-------------------------|----------------------|---------------| | **Pre-transition** | Until navigation triggered | Old page fully visible, no new content yet | Normal reading of old page content | No special handling needed | — | | **Transition in progress (sync mode)** | ~300ms (slide) / ~200ms (fade) | Both pages in DOM: old animating out, new animating in | Only NEW page should be readable; OLD page must have `aria-hidden="true"` | Apply `aria-hidden="true"` to exiting element via framer-motion callback or React state tracking | SC 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (DOM overlap isolation) | | **Transition complete** | Permanent until next navigation | Only new page visible, fully rendered | "Navigated to [page title]" announced via aria-live; focus on `
` element | `onAnimationComplete` callback triggers focus move + aria-live announcement | SC 4.1.3 Status Messages (route change announcement), SC 2.4.3 Focus Order | | **Reduced motion active** | Permanent while preference set | Instant switch or ≤150ms opacity cross-fade, no spatial movement | Same as above but without animation delay — immediate content availability | `useReducedMotion()` hook returns true; variants use duration: 0 or very short opacity-only transition | SC 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions | ### State communication table for motion preference | Motion Preference | Slide Variant Behavior | Fade Variant Behavior | Rationale | WCAG Citation | |-------------------|----------------------|----------------------|-----------|---------------| | **Default (no preference)** | 300ms horizontal slide: outgoing left, incoming right | 200ms cross-dissolve opacity transition | Designer-specified animation for users without motion sensitivity concerns | SC 2.3.3 (not triggered — no reduced motion preference) | | **`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`** | Instant route switch (duration: 0) OR ≤150ms opacity-only cross-fade with NO horizontal movement | ≤150ms opacity transition (already minimal, but duration reduced from 200ms to ≤150ms for consistency) | Spatial motion animations can trigger vestibular disorders; instant or near-instant transitions eliminate this risk while preserving the visual cue of a page change through brief opacity fade | SC 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions (must disable/reduce motion animation triggered by interaction) | ### Why not just `animation: none`? Simply disabling all animation when `prefers-reduced-motion` is set would create an abrupt, jarring experience where content appears instantly with no visual continuity. The better approach is to **replace** the spatial slide animation with either: 1. An instant switch (duration: 0) — simplest and safest for motion-sensitive users 2. A very short opacity cross-fade (≤150ms) — provides minimal visual continuity without triggering vestibular issues The fade variant is already less problematic since it only involves opacity changes, but we still reduce its duration to ≤150ms when reduced motion is preferred for consistency and extra safety. ### framer-motion `useReducedMotion()` hook framer-motion provides the `useReducedMotion()` hook specifically for this purpose: - Returns `true` when `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is set in system preferences - Returns `false` when no preference or `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` - Returns `null` on initial render (before browser preference can be determined) **Handling the null state:** On first render, default to reduced motion behavior (safer choice). Once the hook resolves to a boolean value, update the animation variants accordingly. This prevents a flash of full animation for users who have set reduced motion preferences. ### WCAG citations - **SC 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions:** Motion animations triggered by user interaction must be disabled or replaced when `prefers-reduced-motion` is set. The slide transition (spatial movement) is the primary concern; the fade transition (opacity only) is secondary but still reduced for consistency. - **SC 4.1.3 Status Messages:** Route change announcements via aria-live region constitute status messages that must be programmatically determinable and announced by assistive technologies. --- ## Visual Accessibility Plan ### Motion sensitivity and vestibular disorders **Primary concern:** The slide transition involves horizontal spatial movement (elements sliding across the viewport), which can trigger vestibular disorders in sensitive users. This is explicitly covered by WCAG SC 2.3.3. **SC 2.3.3 vs SC 2.2.2 distinction:** - **SC 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions:** Applies to motion animations triggered by user interaction (like clicking a link that triggers the slide transition). Must be disabled/reduced when `prefers-reduced-motion` is set. This IS applicable to our component. - **SC 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide:** Applies to auto-playing content that lasts more than 5 seconds and starts automatically without user initiation. Our transitions are user-triggered (not auto-playing) and last only 300ms/200ms (well under 5 seconds), so SC 2.2.2 does NOT apply. However, it's worth noting this distinction in documentation to avoid confusion during audits. ### Animation duration compliance - **Slide variant:** 300ms — Well within the 5-second threshold of SC 2.2.2 (not applicable anyway since user-triggered). For reduced motion users, replaced with instant switch or ≤150ms opacity fade per SC 2.3.3. - **Fade variant:** 200ms — Same compliance status as slide. Reduced to ≤150ms for consistency when `prefers-reduced-motion` is set. ### Focus indicator visibility during transitions During the transition animation, focus indicators must remain visible on any focused element in the incoming page. Since framer-motion applies CSS transforms (translate/opacity), standard browser focus outlines should still render correctly as long as: - The focused element is not `aria-hidden` or `inert` - The transform doesn't clip or obscure the focus ring **Recommendation:** Test that focus rings are visible on interactive elements in the incoming page during its enter animation. If framer-motion's transforms cause clipping, consider applying `overflow: visible` to the motion container or adjusting z-index stacking. ### Color contrast considerations The transition itself does not alter color values — text and UI colors remain consistent between pages. However, if a fade transition causes temporary low-contrast states (e.g., both old and new content partially transparent simultaneously), ensure that at no point during the animation do text elements fall below 4.5:1 contrast against their background. **Mitigation:** With `mode="sync"` in AnimatePresence, both pages are visible simultaneously during cross-fade. Ensure page backgrounds are consistent between routes to avoid contrast issues during overlap. If backgrounds differ significantly, consider using a solid overlay during transition or switching to `mode="wait"` (which has no visual overlap). ### Touch target sizing Not directly affected by transitions — touch targets on each individual page maintain their own 44×44px minimum size per SC 2.5.8. However, ensure that interactive elements in the incoming page are not partially obscured by exiting content during transition (z-index management). ### WCAG citations - **SC 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions:** Motion animation triggered by interaction must respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. - **SC 1.4.3 Contrast Minimum:** Text and UI components must maintain adequate contrast throughout transitions, including any overlap states. - **SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum):** Interactive targets must be at least 24×24 CSS pixels (44×44 recommended) — maintained per-page during transitions. --- ## Content Accessibility Plan ### Screen reader content isolation during DOM overlap **Critical issue:** With framer-motion's `AnimatePresence` in default mode, both the exiting and incoming pages exist in the DOM simultaneously for ~300ms (slide) or ~200ms (fade). Without intervention, a screen reader user could encounter: - Content from BOTH pages being announced - Focusable elements from the old page that are now invisible but still reachable via Tab **Solution:** Apply `aria-hidden="true"` to the exiting page's container element while its exit animation is running. This removes it from the accessibility tree entirely, ensuring only the incoming (new) page is readable by screen readers during transition. Implementation approach: - Track which route key is "active" using React state - Apply `aria-hidden={routeKey !== activeRouteKey}` to each motion.div - Update `activeRouteKey` when a new route begins entering - Alternatively, use framer-motion's `onExitComplete` callback to manage aria-hidden on exiting elements ### Route change announcements via aria-live After the transition completes and focus moves to the new page, provide an additional announcement that explicitly states which page was loaded. This helps screen reader users who may not have been actively focused on a navigation link (e.g., using browser back button). ```html
Navigated to: {document.title}
``` **Why `aria-live="polite"` and not `"assertive"`:** Polite announcements wait for the screen reader to finish its current speech before announcing. Assertive would interrupt — too aggressive for normal page navigation. Since we're also moving focus (which itself triggers a screen reader announcement), polite is appropriate for the supplementary route name announcement. ### Document title updates React Router should update `document.title` on each route change. Screen readers like VoiceOver announce document title changes automatically, providing another signal that navigation has occurred. This works in conjunction with our aria-live region and focus management — not as a replacement. ### Link text quality during transitions Navigation links that trigger page transitions must have descriptive text (not "click here" or "read more"). Since the transition wraps all routes, this is handled at the individual page level, but it's worth noting in documentation that link text quality remains important for screen reader users navigating between pages. ### WCAG citations - **SC 1.3.1 Info and Relationships:** Content from exiting pages must be properly hidden (aria-hidden) during DOM overlap to maintain correct information relationships. - **SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value:** The aria-live region has a clear role; route announcements are programmatically determinable. - **SC 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context):** Navigation links must have descriptive text — maintained per-page during transitions. --- ## Testing Strategy ### Test layers and tools | Layer | Tool/Method | What It Catches | Limitations | |-------|-------------|-----------------|-------------| | Static analysis | eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y | Missing aria-hidden, invalid ARIA attributes in JSX | Cannot verify runtime behavior or focus management | | Runtime scanning | axe-core via Playwright | Computed contrast, missing landmarks, ARIA state correctness at runtime | Cannot test motion preference handling or live region announcements | | Keyboard interaction testing | a11y-test (Playwright real key presses) | Focus traps, keyboard navigation through transitions, Tab order after route change | Cannot verify screen reader announcements | | Manual screen reader testing | NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver | Live region announcements, focus movement, content isolation during transition | Requires human tester; It manages two transition variants: "slide" (300ms horizontal movement, default mode with DOM overlap) and "fade" (200ms cross-dissolve). Four ARIA patterns are involved: motion preference detection via `useReducedMotion()`, content isolation during DOM overlap via `aria-hidden`, focus management post-transition targeting `
`, and route change announcements via `aria-live="polite"`. The component has no direct keyboard interaction model — transitions are triggered by navigation actions. ### Implementation Tasks #### Task 1: Motion preference detection with framer-motion useReducedMotion() Estimated Effort: medium Depends on: none #### Test Strategy for Task 1 - Verify `useReducedMotion()` returns correct value when system preference changes - Verify slide variants use duration: 0 when reduced motion is true or null (initial render) - Verify fade variants use ≤150ms duration when reduced motion is active - Simulate in browser devtools: Chrome DevTools → Rendering tab → "Emulate CSS media feature prefers-reduced-motion" #### Acceptance Criteria for Task 1 - When `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is set, slide transition uses instant switch (duration: 0) or ≤150ms opacity-only cross-fade with NO horizontal movement — WCAG SC 2.3.3 - When reduced motion preference cannot be determined (null initial state), default to reduced motion behavior for safety #### Task 2: DOM overlap handling with aria-hidden on exiting pages Estimated Effort: medium Depends on: Task 1 #### Test Strategy for Task 2 - During exit animation: verify `aria-hidden="true"` is present on the exiting motion.div element - After transition completes: verify `aria-hidden` is absent or undefined on the active page's container - Verify no focusable elements from the old page are reachable via Tab during transition #### Acceptance Criteria for Task 2 - Exiting page has `aria-hidden="true"` applied while its exit animation runs — WCAG SC 1.3.1 Info and Relationships - Incoming/active page does NOT have aria-hidden — must remain fully accessible in a11y tree - No race condition where both pages simultaneously lack or have aria-hidden #### Task 3: Post-navigation focus management and route announcement Estimated Effort: medium Depends on: Tasks 1, 2 #### Test Strategy for Task 3 - After route change completes: verify `document.activeElement` is the `
` element of the new page - Verify "Navigated to [page title]" appears in aria-live region and is announced by screen reader - Verify Tab after transition moves through only the new page's interactive elements (not old/exiting content) #### Acceptance Criteria for Task 3 - After route change, focus moves to `
` of new page — WCAG SC 2.4.3 Focus Order - Route change announced via `aria-live="polite"` region after transition completes — WCAG SC 4.1.3 Status Messages #### Task 4: Integration testing and edge case handling Estimated Effort: medium Depends on: Tasks 1, 2, 3 #### Test Strategy for Task 4 - Rapid successive navigations: click multiple links before transition completes → verify focus/aria-hidden state doesn't get confused - Browser back/forward button usage → same focus management applies via React Router route changes - Initial page load (no previous page) → AnimatePresence handles gracefully with no exit animation #### Acceptance Criteria for Task 4 - All four tasks work cohesively without race conditions during rapid navigations — WCAG SC 2.1.1 Keyboard - Reduced motion preference persists across all route changes — WCAG SC 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions ### Failure Modes This plan prevents the following accessibility anti-patterns: 1. **Motion animation not respecting user preference:** Without `useReducedMotion()`, vestibular disorder users experience jarring spatial slide animations that can cause nausea or dizziness. The plan mandates detection and replacement with instant switch or ≤150ms opacity fade. 2. **Focus stranded in invisible exiting content:** After navigation, focus remains on elements from the old page that are now visually hidden but still focusable via Tab. This creates a "keyboard trap" where users cannot reach new page content without extensive reverse-tabbing. The plan mandates moving focus to `
` after transition completes. 3. **Screen reader reading both pages during DOM overlap:** With framer-motion's default AnimatePresence mode, both old and new pages exist in the DOM simultaneously for ~300ms. Without `aria-hidden` on the exiting page, screen readers announce content from BOTH pages, creating confusion about which page is active. The plan mandates aria-hidden isolation. 4. **No announcement of route change:** Screen reader users have no indication that navigation has occurred unless they actively explore the new content. This is especially problematic for browser back/forward button usage where focus wasn't on a link before navigation. The plan mandates an `aria-live="polite"` region announcing "Navigated to [page title]". 5. **Reduced motion treated as binary disable:** Simply setting all animations to duration: 0 when reduced motion is preferred creates jarring instant content swaps with no visual continuity. The plan specifies replacing spatial slide animation with either instant switch OR ≤150ms opacity cross-fade, preserving minimal visual feedback without triggering vestibular issues. 6. **Initial render flash of full animation:** `useReducedMotion()` returns null on first render before the browser preference is determined. Defaulting to full animation (instead of reduced motion) causes a brief flash of spatial movement for users who have set reduced motion preferences. The plan mandates defaulting to reduced motion behavior when the hook value is null. 7. **Focus management timing mismatch:** Moving focus during exit animation (before new page is ready) or not waiting for enter animation completion can result in focus on an element that's still animating/opacity-changing, creating a confusing experience. The plan specifies using `onAnimationComplete` callback to ensure focus moves only after the new page is fully rendered and visible.
